title: Controlled microbial culture
summary: Pasteur's liquid-media culture methods enabled microorganisms to be grown under controlled laboratory conditions.

parents.reason: Experiments connecting microbes to fermentation motivated controlled growth in nutrient media.

title: Isolation of pure microbial cultures
summary: Koch maintained isolated anthrax cultures to connect a particular organism with a particular disease.

parents.reason: Controlled culture provides the growth conditions used to isolate a single microbial population.

title: Isolation of pneumococcus
summary: Sternberg and Pasteur isolated the bacterium later used in pneumococcal disease and transformation experiments.

parents.reason: Culturing permits the organism to be isolated and propagated.
Microscopic inspection distinguishes the isolated bacterial forms.
parents.directContribution: Optical inspection directly characterizes the cultured organisms; nutrient culture separately propagates them for isolation.

title: Griffith's bacterial transformation experiment
summary: Killed virulent pneumococci transferred a stable virulent trait to living nonvirulent pneumococci.

parents.reason: Pneumococcal isolates provide the contrasting strains used in the experiment.
Separate strain cultures permit controlled mixing and recovery of transformed bacteria.

title: Identification of deoxyribose in DNA
summary: Levene identified the sugar distinguishing DNA from ribose-containing nucleic acid.

parents.reason: Isolated nucleic acid supplies the material analyzed for its sugar component.

title: Dische's DNA chemical assay
summary: A diphenylamine color reaction helped distinguish and measure deoxyribose-containing DNA.

parents.reason: Deoxyribose supplies the chemical feature detected by the assay.

title: Chamberland bacterial filtration
summary: Porous porcelain filtration removed bacteria from liquids while allowing smaller infectious agents to pass.

parents.reason: A porous ceramic element supplies the physical filtration barrier.
Culture tests determine whether the filtrate still contains growing bacteria.

title: Laboratory attenuation for vaccines
summary: Pasteur's chicken-cholera work developed weakened microbial preparations that retained protective activity.

parents.reason: Repeated growth and controlled handling permit changes in microbial virulence.
Earlier protective inoculation established the goal of inducing immunity without severe disease.

title: Toxoid preparation
summary: Chemical inactivation rendered bacterial toxins less harmful while preserving their immunizing properties.

parents.reason: Antitoxin assays measure whether modified toxin still elicits protective recognition.
Bacteria-free toxin-containing filtrates provide material for controlled inactivation.

title: Virus cultivation in embryonated eggs
summary: Goodpasture's embryo-based culture work supplied living tissue for growing viruses used in vaccine research.

parents.reason: Recognition of filterable infectious agents motivated cultivation in living host tissue.
Sterile tissue-handling methods limit bacterial contamination during inoculation.

title: Identification of hepatitis B surface antigen
summary: The Australia antigen provided a detectable surface protein later linked to hepatitis B infection.

parents.reason: Serological antigen–antibody reactions reveal the unusual serum antigen.

title: Stabilized prefusion RSV antigen
summary: Structure-guided stabilization preserved RSV's prefusion F protein as a potent vaccine antigen.

parents.reason: Protein structures identify the prefusion conformation to preserve.
Engineered expression produces the stabilized antigen constructs.

title: Oka-strain varicella vaccine
summary: Serial tissue-culture passage produced the attenuated Oka strain used in varicella and later shingles vaccines.

parents.reason: Serial growth in cultured cells supplies the attenuation route.
Earlier attenuation methods established weakened live organisms as protective preparations.

title: Engineered viral gene vectors
summary: Engineered viral DNA supplied a route for carrying selected genetic sequences into cells.

parents.reason: Joining DNA from different sources creates a viral construct with an added payload.

title: Recombinant AAV gene vectors
summary: Recombinant adeno-associated viral constructs delivered foreign genes into mammalian cells.

parents.reason: Viral payload delivery provides the vector strategy adapted to AAV.

title: Engineered oncolytic viruses
summary: Genetically altered herpesvirus was investigated for selective replication in and destruction of tumors.

parents.reason: Engineered viral constructs permit selective replication and payload changes.
The need to attack tumors selectively motivated virus-based therapeutic investigation.

title: CRISPR adaptive immunity in bacteria
summary: Phage-challenge experiments showed that acquired CRISPR spacers protect bacteria against matching viruses.

parents.reason: Bacterial viruses provide controlled infection challenges.
Spacer sequences identify the acquired genetic records matching the attacking phage.

title: Fluorescent antibody labeling
summary: Coons linked fluorescent dyes to antibodies to locate specific biological targets optically.

parents.reason: Specific antibody binding selects the biological target.
Fluorescence optics detects the attached marker.

title: Voltage-clamp recording
summary: Feedback-controlled electrodes held membrane voltage steady while measuring ionic currents.

parents.reason: Sensitive electrical measurement permits small biological currents to be recorded.

title: Nuclear reprogramming by transplantation
summary: Gurdon showed that differentiated cell nuclei could direct development when transferred into enucleated eggs.

parents.reason: Micromanipulation directly places donor nuclei into enucleated eggs.

title: Pancreatic cause of diabetes
summary: Pancreas-removal experiments established a connection between the organ and diabetes.

parents.reason: Knowledge of pancreatic anatomy permits controlled removal and comparison.

title: Intestinal sodium–glucose cotransport
summary: Crane described coupled sodium and glucose transport underlying intestinal glucose absorption.

parents.reason: A selective cell membrane supplies the boundary across which coupled transport occurs.

title: Selective membrane dialysis
summary: Graham used selective membrane passage to separate small dissolved substances from larger colloidal material.

parents.reason: Solution analysis measures which dissolved substances cross the membrane.

title: Piezoelectric effect
summary: The Curie brothers found that mechanical stress generates electric charge in certain crystals.

parents.reason: Charge-sensitive measurement detects electricity produced by stressed crystals.

title: Photomultiplier tube
summary: Successive electron multiplication amplified weak optical signals into measurable currents.

parents.reason: Incident photons release the initial photoelectrons.
An evacuated electronic device transports and multiplies the electron signal.

title: Electronic scintillation counting
summary: Light flashes from radiation interactions were amplified and counted electronically.

parents.reason: Electron multiplication converts faint scintillation flashes into electrical pulses.
Ionizing emissions supply events used to test and calibrate the detector.

title: Computational sequence alignment
summary: Dynamic-programming methods aligned biological sequences to identify related positions.

parents.reason: Optimal subproblem reuse determines the best scoring alignment.
Known protein sequences supply biological strings for comparison.

title: DNA sequence assembly
summary: Computational overlap reconstruction combined fragment reads into longer DNA sequences.

parents.reason: Read sequences supply the fragments to be assembled.
Sequence comparison identifies compatible overlaps between reads.

title: Recurrent neural networks
summary: Feedback connections gave neural networks a state that could persist across successive inputs.

parents.reason: Weighted neural units supplied components extended with recurrent connections.

title: Gradient descent
summary: Cauchy's method iteratively adjusted variables in a direction reducing a differentiable objective.

parents.reason: Partial derivatives determine the direction of local objective change.

title: Binary search trees
summary: An ordered branching data structure supported searching by progressively narrowing key ranges.

parents.reason: Addressable storage implements linked search nodes and key comparisons.

title: Linked lists
summary: Explicit links connected stored records without requiring adjacent memory locations.

parents.reason: Addressable memory stores records and the references connecting them.

title: Recursion in programming
summary: Self-invoking procedures expressed solutions through smaller instances of the same problem.

parents.reason: Recursive function definitions supply a formal model for self-referential computation.

title: Modern predicate logic
summary: Frege's quantified logic formalized statements about objects, properties, and relations.

parents.reason: Deductive mathematical arguments motivated a precise symbolic language for inference.

title: Pauli's neutrino hypothesis
summary: Pauli proposed an unseen neutral particle to account for missing energy in beta decay.

parents.reason: Beta-decay measurements supply the unexplained energy distribution.
Energy balance motivates an additional particle carrying the missing energy.

title: Bohr atomic model
summary: Quantized electron orbits accounted for characteristic hydrogen spectral lines.

parents.reason: A central nucleus supplies the atom's electrostatic structure.
Measured hydrogen wavelengths constrain the predicted energy differences.

title: Joule–Thomson effect
summary: Joule and Thomson measured temperature changes when gas expands through a restriction without external work.

parents.reason: Energy and enthalpy relationships explain the throttling experiment.

title: Liquid helium production
summary: Kamerlingh Onnes liquefied helium, opening an experimental route to extremely low temperatures.

parents.reason: Regenerative expansion cooling supplies a step in helium liquefaction.

title: Boolean switching-circuit theory
summary: Shannon showed how Boolean algebra describes relay circuits for symbolic switching and computation.

parents.reason: Boolean operations model the on/off behavior of interconnected switches.
Relay-based electrical signaling provides physical switches whose combinations can be analyzed.

title: Semiconductor band theory
summary: Wilson's band model explained conduction differences among metals, semiconductors, and insulators.

parents.reason: Quantum electron states in solids produce allowed bands and energy gaps.

title: ABC programming language
summary: ABC provided an interactive language with readable blocks and high-level data operations.

parents.reason: Block-structured control supplies the organization of its executable statements.

title: ID3 decision-tree learning
summary: Quinlan's ID3 selected informative attributes to grow classification trees from labeled examples.

parents.reason: Entropy and information gain determine the attribute-selection criterion.

title: Identification of progesterone
summary: Isolation of the corpus-luteum hormone identified a chemical regulator of reproduction.

parents.reason: Identifying ovarian corpus-luteum tissue provides material for extracting the hormone.

title: Orally active progestin synthesis
summary: Synthesis of norethisterone supplied an orally active progestin later used in contraceptive pills.

parents.reason: Progesterone's biological activity defines the effect sought in an orally effective compound.
Defined steroid connectivity guides the chemical modifications made during synthesis.

title: Identification of the cell nucleus
summary: Brown identified recurring nuclei as structures within plant cells.

parents.reason: Microscopic examination reveals the nucleus within prepared plant cells.

title: Gel electrophoresis
summary: Gel matrices enabled size-dependent separation of biological macromolecules in an electric field.

parents.reason: Electric-field-driven molecular transport supplies the separation force.

title: Ethidium DNA fluorescence assay
summary: Enhanced fluorescence after ethidium binds nucleic acid provided a sensitive DNA-measurement signal.

parents.reason: Intercalation into duplex nucleic acid explains the enhanced bound-dye fluorescence.

title: Golgi's neural staining method
summary: Silver-based staining revealed detailed outlines of a small fraction of neurons in tissue.

parents.reason: Microscopic imaging resolves the stained neuron processes.

title: Proteinase K characterization
summary: A robust fungal protease supplied an enzyme for digesting proteins during biochemical analysis.

parents.reason: Controlled activity measurements characterize the protease's substrate degradation.

title: Identification of the malaria parasite
summary: Laveran identified parasites in the blood of malaria patients.

parents.reason: Blood microscopy reveals the organisms associated with disease.

title: Mustard-gas suppression of blood cells
summary: Blood and bone-marrow injury after gas exposure supplied evidence later used to investigate cytotoxic cancer drugs.

parents.reason: Blood-cell examination detects the leukocyte depletion associated with exposure.

title: Antisense RNA gene-perturbation experiments
summary: Sense and antisense RNA injections were tested for targeted gene suppression in nematodes.

parents.reason: Complementary sequences specify the RNA target under investigation.
Defined gene-derived constructs supply the experimental RNA sequences.
